transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because... things have just felt a bit off lately. 

The things that usually make me feel like myself, they just started feeling... flat. And heavy. Like, I used to go on these photography walks, or help out mentoring the kids. Even just keeping a clean calendar, which I usually like doing. But... I don't know, I just stopped initiating them. 

So... yeah. That's mainly it.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... I guess it's been about a year and three months. Give or take. 

It kind of started... well, a family member had some health issues. Their behavior changed, and... I just had to take on a lot more of the coordination for them. So... around then.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your sleep patterns since you started feeling this way?

My appetite is mostly the same, I guess. But... sleep has been a little different. 

Um... there have been nights where I only sleep maybe two or three hours. I'll wake up before dawn and... I don't really feel tired. I just get up and feel ready to start working. You know, answering emails or updating the appointment lists for the office. 

So... yeah. Just that.
During those times when you wake up early and feel ready to start working, do you also feel unusually energetic, talkative, or like your thoughts are racing?

Um... I don't know about talkative. I'm usually pretty quiet. But... energetic, I guess. 

During those stretches, I just... I start doing a lot. Rebuilding work templates, making care plans for my family member, emailing relatives, reorganizing files... just all at once. 

It's just... if I sit still, it feels like I'm dropping the ball. So I just keep going.

During those periods of high energy and productivity, have you ever felt so 'revved up' that your work or social life was severely disrupted, or that others had to step in because your behavior became concerning?

Um... no, not severely disrupted, I don't think. Nobody's had to step in. 

I mean, work is... mostly fine. Though I guess I've missed a few small things on the calendar lately. Just... having to double-check tasks that I usually do automatically. 

And... socially... I don't know. I guess I haven't been going to my photography group as much. Or doing my mentoring. I just... I don't feel like I'm really there when I go, so I've just been pulling back a bit. But that's about it.

During these past fifteen months, have there been any two-week periods where you felt so low or hopeless that you had significant trouble functioning, eating, or sleeping, or lost interest in almost everything you usually enjoy?

Um... no. Not really. 

I don't think I've felt... hopeless like that. I mean, I still go to work and do what I need to do, so... no. I haven't had anything like that.
During those times when you felt unusually energetic and productive, did that feeling last for at least four days in a row?

Um... I'm not really sure. I don't really track the days like that. 

It just... it happens for a bit, and then it doesn't. I couldn't tell you if it was exactly four days in a row.
Looking back at the last year and three months, would you say that your mood has been low or 'flat' for most of the days, for the majority of the time?

Um... no. I wouldn't say that. 

I don't think my mood has been low most of the time. Just... normal, mostly. I just go about my day.

During those times when you feel that surge of energy and productivity, do you find that your mood feels distinctly 'up', or 'high', or perhaps irritable, as opposed to just feeling like you have a lot of work to get done?

Um... I guess so. Sometimes I have these stretches where I feel... pretty upbeat. Like everything is just clicking at work. 

But... then, I don't know, a tiny change happens... like someone moving a meeting... and I can get a bit sharp with people. It kind of surprises me when I do that. But... yeah. I guess my mood is a bit different then.
